blockers.issue: Slugs are derived only from type plus normalized display name, while trailing disambiguators are stripped. Distinct same-type entities such as common track titles or artists/projects with the same name collapse to the same cache path, so the crawler can skip or overwrite the wrong node; AgentInput.disambiguator is not incorporated anywhere in canonicalization.

validateForEmit receives a single researchToolCalls counter and only enforces total >= 2, so two web_search calls and zero fetch_page calls satisfy the gate even though the contract requires at least one search and one page fetch before emit_node.

emit_node validates citation shape only by checking that at least one citation has a URL string; it does not verify that citations came from Tavily/Firecrawl results, were actually fetched, or match the facts used. A malicious or low-quality page can steer the model into emitting forged citations and still pass the disk path.

fetch_page returns raw untrusted page markdown directly into the agent context without an injection boundary or instruction to treat page text as data. Prompt injection in a scraped page can target emit_node, and the downstream validator has no provenance checks to contain it.

maxNodes is checked without an atomic reservation around cache.write. With concurrent workers, multiple completed agent runs can all observe remaining budget and then write, causing the cache to exceed maxNodes.

loadPending marks pendingLoaded before the async read completes and pendingReverses is otherwise mutated/flushed outside a global lock. Concurrent writes can proceed against an empty or stale pending map and later overwrite or lose pending reverse updates.

Edge fields use a generic EdgeRef schema with no field-specific target-type constraints. For example, track.samples can point to an artist and pass validation; reverse materialization then writes sampled_by onto a non-track target where schema parsing strips it, violating reverse-edge invariants.

The system prompt explicitly tells the model to emit a best-guess node with a short limited-information article when it cannot resolve an entity, contradicting the abandon_node flow and creating a prompt-level escape hatch toward stub or hallucinated nodes.

warnings.issue: runLocked stores next.catch(...) but compares against a newly-created catch promise in finally, so lock entries are never deleted. Serialization still chains, but long crawls leak one lock promise per touched slug.

--heartbeat-webhook accepts and fetches an arbitrary URL with no scheme, host, or allowlist validation. If this CLI is ever wrapped by a service or fed untrusted arguments, it becomes an SSRF/internal-callback primitive.
The cache assertion allows up to 40% of materialized nodes to have no citations, so the post-run harness does not enforce the same citation floor as emit_node.
The persisted schema accepts editorial_article with min length 1 and citations as an empty array. That makes NodeCache.write a weak final disk guard if any caller bypasses runAgent.

The emit_node tool description still says the third attempt accepts the best payload as-is, while the implementation is strict. This stale instruction can push the model toward behavior the code will reject.

summary: FAIL: the current Phase 1 path has real correctness and strictness gaps despite passing typecheck and the non-live test suite. The most serious issues are slug collisions from type+name-only keys, insufficient research and citation provenance enforcement around emit_node, raw tool-output prompt injection exposure, non-atomic crawl budget enforcement, races in the pending reverse-edge cache state, and schema gaps that allow semantically invalid edge targets. The remaining warnings are mostly hardening issues around lock cleanup, webhook URL handling, and disk-level strictness.
